root_motivation: morsel is the missing-middle Rust crate for embedded ML — but the load-bearing piece for adoption is the offline `bake` CLI that turns trained weights into Rust source. Without bake, every consumer crate has to hand-write const arrays from numpy dumps. Phase 0a ships only the bake CLI; the runtime nn::Lstm/Conv1d/LogMel primitives are Phase 0b. Carving out bake first means the file format and emission shape are locked before the runtime primitives are designed against them.
user_persona: model author (jsy or future-Claude on jsy's behalf) running the bake CLI once per trained model, offline, after `safetensors` export. Output is a `weights.rs` file that gets committed into a consumer crate.

unfakeable_metric.name: acceptance_tests_passing
unfakeable_metric.harness_command: cargo test --tests 2>&1 | grep -E 'test result: ok' | wc -l

acceptance_criteria.description: `morsel-bake --in <safetensors-file> --arch <name> --out <rust-file>` reads tensors from the safetensors file, emits Rust source containing one `pub const NAME: [[f32; N]; M] = ...;` (or 1-D `[f32; N]`) per tensor, plus `pub const ARCH_FINGERPRINT: &str = "<arch>-<dim-summary>-v1";`. Exit 0 on success.

Const arrays preserve f32 precision exactly — round-tripping (write tensor → safetensors → bake → const → parse from emitted source) yields bit-identical f32 bytes. Use Rust's `{:e}` or `f32::from_bits` style if needed to avoid lossy formatting.
The emitted `.rs` file compiles standalone (no morsel runtime deps). The test writes the output to a tempdir, wraps it in a minimal `Cargo.toml`+`lib.rs`, runs `cargo build`, and asserts success.

Tensor names from safetensors that contain `.` or `/` are sanitized to uppercase Rust-identifier-safe names (`weight.ih` → `WEIGHT_IH`, `layer/0/weight` → `LAYER_0_WEIGHT`). Conflicts after sanitization → exit 4 with stderr listing the colliding names.
Tensors with dtype other than f32 → exit 5 with stderr listing the offending tensor and its dtype, and the message `only f32 supported in Phase 0a`. (f16/bf16/int8 are Phase 0b with --quant flag.)

Tensors with rank > 2 are emitted as Rust nested arrays one dimension deeper per rank (`[[[f32; D2]; D1]; D0]`). Rank-0 (scalar) tensors emit `pub const NAME: f32 = ...;`. Rank > 4 → exit 6 with stderr `rank N exceeds supported max 4`.
Non-existent --in file → exit 2 with stderr containing the path and `safetensors file not found`. --out path that already exists → exit 7 unless `--force` is passed (then overwrites).

Emitted file includes a `//! generated by morsel-bake v<crate-version> from <input-basename> @ <RFC3339>` doc header. The header is excluded from any byte-level diff testing (commented out via `cfg`-style sentinels), so re-baking the same input produces a stable file modulo the header.

scope: Sanitize tensor names to Rust idents
Emit Rust source with const arrays preserving f32 bit-exactness
Emit ARCH_FINGERPRINT const with arch name + dim summary
Smoke build of emitted code in a tempdir
non_goals: Loading the model and running inference — that's the morsel runtime, Phase 0b
ONNX, PyTorch native, GGUF, or any other format
Library primitives (nn::Lstm, nn::Conv1d, nn::LogMel) — all Phase 0b

five_whys_trace.q: Why bake-CLI as Phase 0a separate from nn::Lstm/Conv1d/LogMel runtime primitives?
five_whys_trace.a: Because bake's output format is the contract — once locked, the runtime can be designed against it. Building runtime first risks designing primitives that the baker can't faithfully produce.

five_whys_trace.q: Why safetensors input rather than PyTorch state_dict?
five_whys_trace.a: Because safetensors is the modern HF-blessed format, has a clean Rust crate, and is dtype-explicit. PyTorch pickle is unsafe (literally — arbitrary code execution on load) and requires Python in the loop.

Because the same trained model must produce identical outputs whether loaded by morsel's runtime or by the original PyTorch eval — any precision loss in baking shows up as silent inference drift, the worst kind of bug.

five_whys_trace.q: Why smoke-build the emitted code in tests (AC3)?
five_whys_trace.a: Because const-array syntax has subtle errors (trailing commas, type inference quirks for nested) that only surface at compile time. Without a smoke build, a regression in the emitter could ship code that doesn't compile until the consumer's CI catches it.
